Replay

Authenticated checkpoint transfer

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
EmbeddingAuthorization and commitBounds and lifecycleRemaining integration

Use replay/provision/checkpoint to publish or retrieve a room checkpoint through authenticated upload, download and status operations. It connects those operations to durable room storage. It reuses replay/transfer for bounded, retriable chunks. A per-room Server borrows the existing authority service and a typed storage backend; a Client borrows the registered process's control connection. Ordinary transfer operations grant no authority. Protocol 2 adds a separate guarded restore decision for an exact durable publication. Protocol 3 adds complete external asset packages under the same authenticated publication and restore lifecycle.

Embedding#

Odin
// Keep these owners at stable addresses and serialize their calls.
backend: storage.Checkpoint_Backend(World, Control, Action, Event, SEATS)
endpoint: checkpoint.Server
backend = {&store, game_model()}
ok := checkpoint.server_open(
    &endpoint, &room.service, storage.checkpoint_backend(&backend), control_wire,
)

Check ok before routing packets. The backend model is selected by the deployment; the request cannot select code or schemas. Multiplex server_receive beside authority/provisioning handlers and call server_update every frame. Close the checkpoint endpoint before its authority service or Store. It never polls/drains the shared wire itself. Multiple rooms need separately bounded endpoint owners.

checkpoint.Hub manages that bounded endpoint inventory for a provisioning Hub. Open it with one deployment-selected Backend after the provisioning hub opens, route hub_receive, call hub_update after admission processing, and close it before its provisioning owner. It mirrors only already-admitted resident rooms; unknown-room checkpoint traffic never creates or restarts a coordinator. Room slots remain stable for the provisioning owner's lifetime. A poisoned hub refuses routing.

Data uses reliable delivery by default so it works on WebSocket/TLS. An embedding with an authenticated confidential datagram transport may explicitly select data_channel = .Unreliable on both endpoints; blob retransmission then handles loss, duplication and reordering. Control requests/replies always use reliable delivery. Selecting a channel the underlying transport does not support fails to make progress; there is no implicit transport downgrade.

The client first registers through the existing authority RPC on the same connection, then opens with its control key, clock and borrowed transport. Build a Request with its identity, process nonce, current coordinator generation, room/content, model contract and a nonzero operation sequence. Keep operation sequences increasing within that process; control request retries reuse the entire request. These sequences are separate from lease/RPC and gameplay action sequences.

  • Upload supplies the exact checkpoint Point, immutable bytes and expected publication revision (zero initially). client_begin copies the upload bytes.
  • Status supplies a zero Point/revision and returns current publication metadata. An absent save returns Missing.
  • Download supplies a zero Point and the exact publication revision from status. A replacement publication returns Stale, allowing a fresh status decision.

Route client_receive from the shared wire and call client_update; continue ordinary authority renewals independently. Complete upload means a durable publication receipt, not merely chunk delivery. A completed download owns its bytes in client.saved until the next begin or close. client_decode requires the game model before exposing a decoded checkpoint. An application must still prepare assets and obtain a fresh authority permit before restoring simulation.

Authorization and commit#

Every control message and transfer packet is HMAC-SHA256 authenticated with the member's control key. Domain and direction separation cover the whole canonical envelope. Data also names the exact request hash, identity/nonce, coordinator generation, operation sequence and transfer ID. HMAC supplies integrity and member authentication, not secrecy: the embedding must use verified TLS, or an isolated local test channel. No private enrollment Bundle or bearer game token is returned.

The server requires an enabled, currently registered identity and nonce on the bound transport peer and connection generation. Status/download/upload all require can_host and trusted_authority; dedicated policy additionally requires infrastructure. A normal player cannot obtain an authority-only archive.

A new upload requires a live owner lease in the checkpoint epoch. Permission is rechecked while receiving, when the archive completes, and through a Commit_Guard after typed validation and SQL update immediately before commit. If validation or storage waiting outlives the lease, the transaction rolls back. The backend also compares the complete durable coordinator Record and publication revision, fencing a competing service process. A custom backend must honor the same atomicity, model validation and commit-guard contract; an in-memory callback that merely returns success is not durable publication.

The currently stored exact publisher/Point/contract can be acknowledged after a lost reply without a new write or live owner lease. Current trusted registration is still required. This permits recovery of a commit result without reactivating its former host. Old revisions cease to be retry targets after replacement.

Bounds and lifecycle#

One transfer is active per endpoint, with at most a 1 MiB archive. Upload allocates only the declared, validated checkpoint size. Download retains one owned archive. The shared transfer engine limits chunks, retransmits missing data, checks SHA and envelope integrity, and times out after 30 seconds. Endpoint destruction, timeout, registration loss or revoked permissions releases its transfer state. An expired upload owner also releases its slot, so it cannot block its successor's publication.

Authenticated ingress has a per-room bucket of 64 packets, replenished at 128/s; control operations have per-member buckets of eight, replenished at four/s. Malformed traffic performs no storage load or transfer allocation. The embedding must also bound connections and packets per frame before dispatching.

An explicitly newer operation from the same registered process may supersede its transfer. This also handles a download whose final acknowledgement was lost. Another member cannot evict an in-flight transfer; a changed request at the same sequence cannot replace it. Old signed chunks cannot cross the new request hash or transfer binding. Status and exact publication acknowledgement do not replace an ongoing transfer or grant a lease. An uncertain write result is resolved through status or an exact retry, never an assumed fresh publication.

An exact Status retry reuses its bounded cached read result while current membership/connection checks still pass. A new request sequence obtains a fresh publication view. This avoids repeated expensive model/asset validation blocking authority renewal while a read reply is in flight.

The native SQLite API retains its previous names as aliases for the shared Publication/Saved metadata types. Their serialized field layout is unchanged. Checkpoint protocol 3 includes Restore and signed package descriptors, with a v3 HMAC domain. Earlier transfer clients and services must be upgraded together; there is no silent wire fallback. Publication metadata remains version 1; gameplay, authority RPC, Bundle/Record and archive formats are unchanged. The protocol package also checks for WASM.

Remaining integration#

The standalone room service registers deployment-selected Cavecrawl, Speedball and Scrapyard backends through the bounded checkpoint Hub. Native TLS gates verify each actual game model across service restart. Room/Party save handling owns status, capture, publication and retries, with native/browser Cavecrawl acceptance. Room/Party drives the full guarded restore lifecycle, with actual Cavecrawl resume/retry UI and native/browser acceptance. Other game paths and durable external assets beyond the bounded package profile still need integration. Scrapyard declares and validates its current/pending spray dependencies. Download alone grants no authority. See the broader all-members-gone recovery plan.
